title: Quasi-coherent scheme modules on the big fppf site
statement: Fix universes and small sites as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $V$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and put $\mathcal C_V=(\mathit{Sch}/V)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], with ring sheaf $\mathcal O(u:T\to V)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. For a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_V$-module $M$ [pqf-def-coherent], define $A_V(M)(u:T\to V)=\Gamma(T,u^*M)$, with restriction along $h:T'\to T$ given by section pullback and the canonical identification $h^*u^*M\simeq(uh)^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For a module map $v:M\to N$ put $A_V(v)_u=\Gamma(T,u^*v)$. These formulas define an equivalence from quasi-coherent Zariski modules to quasi-coherent module sheaves on $\mathcal C_V$, with all module maps; modules mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and site quasi-coherence means local presentations by arbitrary small free modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Its inverse is restriction to Zariski open subschemes, and the unit and counit are the canonical section comparisons, equal to the identity on these opens. For every scheme map $f:T\to V$, restriction of $A_V(M)$ to $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ is canonically $A_T(f^*M)$, naturally in $M$, compatibly with identity and composition of base maps. The functor $A_V$ into all module sheaves preserves small colimits; in particular $A_V(\operatorname{Coker}v)\simeq\operatorname{Coker}(A_V(v))$, where both cokernels are formed in the ambient module categories. There are canonical isomorphisms $A_V(\mathcal O_V)\simeq\mathcal O$ and $A_V(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_V}N)\simeq A_V(M)\otimes_{\mathcal O}A_V(N)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The inverse tensor comparison sends local section tensors to their tensor sections after pullback. No finiteness, Noetherian, separatedness or flatness condition is imposed on $V,M,N$ or $f$.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent)(1), including the associated-sheaf formula and restriction inverse from lemma-fully-faithful-associated; Tag 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial)(1); Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits)(3),(4),(7). Only right exactness, not exactness, is asserted for the big-site functor.

proof.text: First the displayed section rule is an fppf sheaf, without sheafifying it. For $u:T\to V$, the module $u^*M$ is quasi-coherent by pullback preservation. For an fppf cover $\{h_i:T_i\to T\}$, it is an fpqc cover. A compatible family of sections of $h_i^*u^*M$ is a compatible family of module maps $\mathcal O_{T_i}\to h_i^*u^*M$. Full faithfulness of fpqc descent gives a unique map $\mathcal O_T\to u^*M$, hence a unique glued section. This also applies to $M=\mathcal O_V$, giving the ring sheaf in the statement. Scalar actions glue because all restrictions are semilinear. The pullback identity and composition identifications make this a presheaf: their composites agree on local tensors $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto ab\otimes m$, and module maps commute with this formula.

Apply the big-to-small ringed comparison to $S=V$. Write $L_V=\epsilon_V^*$ and $R_V=\epsilon_{V,*}$. Since the presheaf in step 1 is already a sheaf, its sheafification comparison identifies $L_VM$ with exactly $A_V(M)$, on objects, maps and restrictions. The ringed-topos module adjunction gives $L_V\dashv R_V$, and a left adjoint preserves every existing small colimit. The tensor formula gives $L_V\mathcal O_V=\mathcal O\otimes_{\epsilon_V^{-1}\mathcal O_V}\epsilon_V^{-1}\mathcal O_V\simeq\mathcal O$ by multiplication. On a Zariski open $W$, the comparison unit is the sheafification map on $P_M(W)=M(W)$; step 1 identifies it with the identity. These statements apply with any scheme in place of $V$.

The ambient colimit of a small diagram $(M_i)$ of quasi-coherent scheme modules is quasi-coherent: form the cokernel of $d:\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}M_i\to\bigoplus_iM_i$, whose component at $a$ is inclusion into the $i$ summand minus $M(a)$ followed by inclusion into the $j$ summand. Maps from this cokernel to $H$ are precisely families $M_i\to H$ equal along every arrow, so this is the colimit. Both sums and their cokernel are quasi-coherent by the cited closure statements. Thus step 2 applies to this ambient colimit, proving the asserted small-colimit preservation for $A_V$, including the ambient cokernel comparison.

For $f:T\to V$ and $g:U\to T$, the composition isomorphism gives $\Gamma(U,(fg)^*M)\simeq\Gamma(U,g^*f^*M)$. It commutes with module maps and further section pullback, hence identifies the restricted sheaf $A_V(M)|_{\mathcal C_T}$ with $A_T(f^*M)$. Identity maps give the identity comparison. For successive base maps, the two composite comparisons agree: on local scalar tensors both send $a\otimes(b\otimes(c\otimes m))$ to $abc\otimes m$; these generate the tensor pullbacks. This proves all the asserted naturality and base-composition compatibilities before using the equivalence.

Choose an affine open cover $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $V$. The affine tilde equivalence identifies $M|_W$ with $\widetilde Q$. Choose a module presentation $B^{(K)}\to B^{(J)}\to Q\to0$ (take generators and then generators of the kernel). The tilde functor preserves colimits and $\widetilde B\simeq\mathcal O_W$, so this gives $\mathcal O_W^{(K)}\to\mathcal O_W^{(J)}\to M|_W\to0$. Applying $L_W$, which preserves sums and cokernels and sends the structure sheaf to the structure sheaf, gives a free presentation on $\mathcal C_W$. For every $T\to V$, apply this argument to $f^*M$ and use step 4; the affine open cover of $T$ is fppf. Thus $A_V(M)$ is site quasi-coherent in the stated local-presentation sense. Finally $R_VA_V(N)=N$ with identity unit by step 2, so adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A_V(M),A_V(N))=\operatorname{Hom}(M,R_VA_V(N))=\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)$ on all module maps.

Let $G$ be site quasi-coherent on $\mathcal C_V$. At the final object $V$, its definition gives an fppf covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ and presentations $\mathcal O^{(K_i)}\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal O^{(J_i)}\to G|_{\mathcal C_{V_i}}\to0$. The scheme free modules $K'_i=\mathcal O_{V_i}^{(K_i)}$, $J'_i=\mathcal O_{V_i}^{(J_i)}$ are quasi-coherent (the structure module is the rank-one case of the affine tilde description). By step 2 their images under $A_{V_i}$ are the two free site modules. Step 5 lifts $d_i$ uniquely to $h_i:K'_i\to J'_i$. Put $F_i=\operatorname{Coker}h_i$, which is quasi-coherent. Step 3 gives an isomorphism $b_i:A_{V_i}(F_i)\simeq G|_{\mathcal C_{V_i}}$ induced by the cokernel projection.

On $V_{ij}=V_i\times_VV_j$, step 4 identifies the images of $p_i^*F_i$ and $p_j^*F_j$ with the restrictions in step 6. Lift $b_j^{-1}b_i$ by step 5 to $\phi_{ij}:p_i^*F_i\to p_j^*F_j$. Lift its inverse also; faithfulness makes their composites identities. On a triple product the image of $\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$ is $(b_k^{-1}b_j)(b_j^{-1}b_i)=b_k^{-1}b_i$, the image of $\phi_{ik}$, so faithfulness proves the cocycle; step 4 supplies the same pullback identifications in both expressions. The covering is fpqc, so effective descent produces a quasi-coherent $F$ and compatible isomorphisms $u_i^*F\simeq F_i$. No intersection of affine opens is being assumed affine, and no finiteness condition on the modules is needed.

proof.text: Compose the descended identifications with $b_i$ to get $A_V(F)|_{\mathcal C_{V_i}}\simeq G|_{\mathcal C_{V_i}}$; they agree on overlaps by the definition of $\phi_{ij}$. The sheaf-Hom gluing statement gives a global map $b:A_V(F)\to G$. Glue the local inverses as well; uniqueness of gluing gives inverse composites, so $b$ is an isomorphism. Restricting to opens and using $R_VA_V(F)=F$ identifies $R_VG\simeq F$, proving that restriction takes $G$ to a quasi-coherent module. The canonical counit $L_VR_VG\to G$ is also an isomorphism: naturality with $b:L_VF\simeq G$ reduces it to the counit at $L_VF$, whose inverse is $L_V$ of the identity unit by the triangle identity. Its open component is the identity by that same unit equation. Hence the specified functors, with these canonical unit and counit maps, are inverse equivalences.

source.place: Tag 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), final gluing paragraph; Tag 0GN7 (lemma-fully-faithful-associated), restriction inverse

proof.text: The scheme tensor $M\otimes N$ is quasi-coherent by the cited tensor-closure statement. Apply the ringed-topos pullback tensor isomorphism to $\epsilon_V$ from step 2 and replace each $L_V$ by $A_V$. This gives the claimed canonical tensor isomorphism, and the structure-sheaf isomorphism was computed in step 2. To specify its inverse, for $u:T\to V$ send $s\otimes t$ to the tensor section of $u^*M\otimes u^*N$, followed by the inverse of $u^*(M\otimes N)\simeq u^*M\otimes u^*N$. The scheme pullback tensor formula shows this respects further section pullback, so these bilinear maps induce a map of tensor sheaves. It is the inverse of the ringed-topos comparison: on local tensor generators the comparison sends $a\otimes(m\otimes n)$ to $(a\otimes m)\otimes(1\otimes n)$ and the displayed map sends this back to $a\otimes(m\otimes n)$; the other composite is the identity by scalar balancing. Sheafification extends these identities from local generators. This also gives the stipulated normalization for tensors of local sections.
